assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening the high-energy neutrino sky is a new observational window built on a remarkable instrument, a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice. It brought a source-identified discovery (diffuse astrophysical flux, the blazar TXS 0506+056, the Galactic plane) with lasting consequences for cosmic-ray origins and multimessenger astronomy. This is the kind of detector-driven discovery I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the only credited name and was the long-term driving force and spokesperson behind IceCube. The credit is clean for a single-laureate configuration, but the discovery was the work of a very large collaboration, and the AMANDA/IceCube instrument lineage and other leaders (for example the experiment's later directors) are not on the supplied list. The prize rules would favour recognising the originator of the concept, but I cannot judge fairness from the list alone.
assessment.maturity: Observed since 2013 and confirmed by independent multi-wavelength follow-up of the 2017 alert and later analyses, with the flux consistent across channels. The interpretation of individual source classes is still evolving, but the discovery itself is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Whether a single-person award is acceptable given the collaboration scale and instrument history.
Source-class attribution of the diffuse flux is not settled; the Galactic plane and TXS results rest on a limited number of sources.
I have not independently verified the details of credit within the collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray bursts by BeppoSAX and the discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows settled the long-standing question of their distance and showed they are cosmological, enormously energetic explosions. This was decisive for the field and is a classic case of instrument capability enabling a discovery.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB monitor and wide-field camera work that delivered arcminute positions and the first X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni led the optical and radio follow-up that fixed the redshift scale. These are complementary and decisive contributions that fit a three-person split. Other optical groups (for example van Paradijs and collaborators) played a role, and one of those key people is deceased, which constrains the configuration.
assessment.maturity: The 1997 discoveries have been confirmed repeatedly by Swift and others over nearly three decades, so recognition is late rather than premature. The physics is stable, with the fireball picture and GRB-supernova connection widely accepted.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the space-instrument teams and the ground-based follow-up groups is contested to some degree.
Some principal contributors on the observation side may not be eligible or may be missing from the supplied names.
I am recalling the historical record from memory rather than verifying it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties around 1e-18 and have become a new standard for timekeeping, relativistic geodesy and fundamental-constant tests. It is a measurement technique that opens a new regime of precision and is as much instrument development as physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised early strontium clocks; Ye brought them to record accuracy and coherence and added many-body and comparisons work. The two-person configuration is natural, although ion-clock and optical-frequency-comb recognition (2005 prize) overlaps in background, and other leaders (Ludlow, Lemke, Schmidt and others) are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Stable, independently reproduced across several laboratories, and moving into redefinition discussions for the second. The work is mature and timely, although the redefinition of the SI second may yet be a decisive event.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition, and with trapped-ion clock contributions not listed.
Credit between lattice-clock proposal and demonstration is clear but other groups made key developments.
I am outside atomic physics and rely on colleagues for deeper judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and the discovery of topological insulators created a field that links band topology, symmetry and robust surface states. Conceptually clean, experimentally confirmed, and with widespread influence on condensed matter physics and quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory, Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe, and Hasan's group demonstrated 3D topological insulators by ARPES. A three-person split omits Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and others whose roles are not on this list; this is a real attribution difficulty and I would want colleagues in condensed matter to guide the final configuration.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is extensive and independent, and the field has stabilised with many materials. Recognition is timely and, if anything, overdue, but it overlaps the 2016 topological-phase prize in subject matter.
uncertainties: Omission of Mele and others would be contentious, and the theory/experiment split is not unique.
Overlap with the 2016 Nobel for topological phase transitions and phases.
Condensed matter is outside my expertise, so I defer to colleagues on the detailed priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a sizeable theta13 mixing angle was the last missing piece of the three-flavour oscillation picture and opened the way to measuring leptonic CP violation. It was a precision experiment in which careful systematics and near/far detector design were decisive.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) reported a definitive observation with reactor antineutrinos; T2K (Nishikawa) reported appearance indications and RENO and Double Chooz were closely parallel. The supplied credit omits the other reactor experiments, so the fair configuration is unresolved, and a prize risks seeming incomplete since 2015 already recognised oscillations.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent confirmations by reactor and accelerator experiments, with the value now precisely known. The result is stable, but its significance is partly as a stepping stone to CP violation measurements not yet complete.
uncertainties: Competing parallel experiments (RENO, Double Chooz, T2K) create difficult credit allocation.
Overlap with the 2015 neutrino oscillation prize may weaken the case.
Whether the scientific significance rises to a stand-alone prize or awaits CP violation results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation peak is a calibrated standard ruler that underpins dark-energy measurements through galaxy surveys, and the detection in SDSS and 2dFGRS was a clear observational milestone with a firm theoretical basis in early-universe plasma physics.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's team (SDSS luminous red galaxies) and the 2dFGRS group (Cole, Percival) detected the peak in 2005. The credit is plausible as a three-person split, but it is not obvious that survey leaders and the theoretical prediction (Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich) are adequately represented, and the Nobel in 2011 and 2019 already covered cosmology.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many subsequent surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI) and now a pillar of precision cosmology. Mature, though the most recent dark-energy hints from DESI are still evolving and are not the credited discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the theory prediction versus the observational detection is split, and the original theorists are not on the list.
Overlap with earlier cosmology prizes (2006, 2011, 2019).
Large-survey collaborations make individual attribution hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré quantum materials with tunable flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity. The combination of a precise theoretical prediction and a striking experiment makes it a clear conceptual and experimental advance with a very active field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. Andrei's group made prior experimental contributions on twisted bilayers; only three names can be chosen and this omits her, a genuine attribution tension, as would Cao and others.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many groups and extended to other moiré systems, so the core finding is solid, but the nature of the superconductivity and the full phase diagram are still debated, so the field may still be developing.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Omission of Andrei, or of Cao as first author, may be disputed.
I am outside condensed matter and defer to colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced precision full-sky microwave background maps that fixed the cosmological parameters of the standard model at percent level and confirmed the geometry and composition of the Universe. It was a flagship instrument-driven result of exceptional importance.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led instrument design and calibration and Spergel led the cosmological analysis, which is a sensible split. But CMB recognition already went to COBE in 2006 and cosmology from supernovae in 2011 and the 2019 prize, and the Planck team's role is not in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Superseded in precision by Planck but fully consistent with it, so confirmed and stable. Recognition is late rather than premature, with the novelty reduced by later missions.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 CMB prize and subsequent cosmological recognition.
Planck and ground-based experiments may be viewed as the stronger comparison.
Large collaboration with many essential contributors.
